beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Naruto Uzumaki learned a forbidden jutsu in one night, and read one line too many. Everything his clones learn, he keeps.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Then he read the Hokage's whole archive and found a roster with one name inked out. He already knows which name fits.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: The next morning, every chair in the Hokage's office is taken. So is the windowsill. So is the ceiling.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Old man. Who was Kushina Uzumaki?

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: The old man doesn't answer for a long time. The pipe in his hand has gone out, and he hasn't noticed.

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: Which one of you is the real one?

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: The one who's not sitting in your hat.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: I'm in the hat, if that helps.

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: Who told you that name?

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Nobody. That's the problem. Everybody I asked changed the subject. The shelf, the roster, my birthday. Even the dust is lying.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Twelve years ago, the Third Hokage made a law. Nobody in Konoha may speak of the Nine-Tails inside Naruto. Not to him, and not to their kids.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Everybody obeyed. It's the loneliest law the village ever wrote, and the man who wrote it is sitting very still.

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: I made that law. I can break it. I'm only asking myself whether I should.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: There's a thousand of us, old man. Sixty in here. The rest are in the corridor, the garden and on the roof. Every one of us is listening.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Ears are pressed to every window of the Hokage Tower. A thousand Narutos, holding their breath at the same time.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: The old man has been lying for twelve years, for reasons he thought were good. Now he's counting his audience. A lie only works on one listener at a time.

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: Your mother was Kushina Uzumaki. Red hair, down to her waist. And a temper the whole village learned to respect.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: She had red hair?

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: Very red. You got her stubbornness. Not her hair.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Before Naruto, the Nine-Tails lived inside Kushina Uzumaki. That part isn't a what-if. It's the first thing the old man admits.

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: And your father was Minato Namikaze. The Fourth Hokage.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: The Fourth Hokage. The face on the mountain, right outside the window. Naruto once painted that face orange. He did it with a bucket and a lot of confidence.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: I painted my dad.

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: You painted him with great enthusiasm. He would have laughed.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Then the old man tells the rest. October tenth. The seal weakened as Naruto was born, and the fox got loose over the village. The Fourth fought it, and sealed it inside his own newborn son.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Neither parent lived to see morning. The old man says it plainly. If he's telling the truth, he'll tell all of it.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: How did it get out?

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: The seal weakens in childbirth. That's all anyone knows.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: The old man braces for shouting. It doesn't come. Naruto has spent a month reading what happens to people who panic. He doesn't.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Why didn't you tell me?

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: Because the village feared the fox, and children repeat what their parents say. I thought silence would keep you safe. I was wrong about the cost.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Nobody moves. Sixty Narutos have stopped fidgeting for the first time in their lives. One of them is holding the old man's hat, very carefully.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: We're here, Boss.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: I'm not gonna yell, old man. I want two things. First, don't lie to me again.

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: Never again. And the second?

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Mom and Dad's mission reports. Everything they ever filed.

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: Those are classified.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: I'm on staff. There's a form.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Section whatever! He signed it twice!

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: I did write that form myself, didn't I.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: No shouting. No revenge. No apology. Naruto has just learned who his parents were, and the first thing he asks for is their paperwork.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Midnight, in the archive. A thousand clones would be too loud, so it's twenty. Two boxes on the back table. Namikaze. Uzumaki, K.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: You open it.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: I'm you. I'm also not ready.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Then we'll open it together.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Okay. On three.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: On three, or after three?

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Why is that hard?! Just open it!

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: The Fourth Hokage's reports are dry, exact and short. Departure time. Route. Enemy strength. Result. He never uses an adjective when a number will do.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Listen to this one. Mission complete. Zero casualties. Zero damage to client property. Client unhappy about the weather.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Here's another. Mission complete. Cause of delay, council meeting. Cause of council meeting, unknown.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: He's so boring. I love him already.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Boss. Border patrol report. It says, nothing happened. Underlined.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: He was proud of nothing. Best sentence ever.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Then, in the margin of a patrol report, the only thing in the box that isn't a number. A doodle. A small steaming bowl, with chopsticks. Ramen.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Boss. He drew ramen. On a patrol report.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Of course he did.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Boss, are you crying?

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: It's dust. This whole archive is dust.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: His father's capital letters lean forward, like he's late for something. Naruto's do too. He's never noticed. He's never had anything to compare them to.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Kushina's box is thicker. It's an incident file. Every wall, fence and window she ever broke, in order, with invoices.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Broken fence, market district. Broken door, Academy. Broken wall, the same wall, twice.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Cause of damage, temper. Cause of damage, temper. Cause of damage, temper, but the other man started it.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Cause of damage, temper. That's my mom.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: It's the first time he's ever spoken the word. It comes out as a joke, so it won't have to be anything else.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Boss, there's a fountain. She broke a fountain.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: How did she do that?

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: It says she was practising something. The fountain was in the way.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: The fountain was in the way. That's so true.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Last page. A man said something rude about her friend. Damages paid in full. Apology, none.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Good. Nobody should apologise for that.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Can we frame the invoices?

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: No. We're framing the invoices.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Clerks say a person's file is who they were on their worst day. Kushina's worst days, Naruto notices, were nearly always for somebody else.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: By morning he has met both of his parents. One was careful, one was loud, and neither of them got to file a report about him. He'll have to write that one himself.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Deeper in the box there's another set of reports. About a team. Three genin and one jonin, written up every week in the same dry hand.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Boss. His students. One of them is called Kakashi Hatake.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Our Kakashi?

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Skilled. Follows every rule. Will need to learn which ones matter.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Team Minato. Kakashi, a boy named Obito Uchiha, and a girl named Rin Nohara. Their teacher writes about them like they're the most interesting things he's ever filed.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Obito Uchiha. Late every single day. Reason given, helped an old woman across the road. Every report. A different old woman.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: A different old woman. Huh.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Naruto has heard excuses like that. This week. From a man with a book, who got lost on the road of life.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: He learned it from Obito.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: He opens his notebook to the eleven dates. Then he finds the last pages of the team's file. Two names. Two dates. Two short reports, as dry and exact as the rest.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Boss. The dates match.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: I know. I counted twice.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Boss. Do we tell the others?

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Tell them what? It's not our name to tell.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Eleven clerks noted that Kakashi was late. Nobody wrote down why, because nobody ever asked.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: The next dawn. Team Seven waits at the training ground. Sasuke glares at the trees. Sakura reads the clouds. Kakashi Hatake is late, as always. Every single time.

beats.speaker: SAKURA
beats.text: He said dawn. It's noon.

beats.speaker: SASUKE
beats.text: He's asleep in a tree somewhere. Ignore him and train.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Give me an hour. Do the wall drill. Don't touch my wires.

beats.speaker: SAKURA
beats.text: Where are you going?

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: To read something.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Past the training grounds stands a black stone covered in names. Every ninja on it died for the village. One man stands before it, hands in his pockets, reading a name he knows by heart.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: In canon, this is why Kakashi is late. Not laziness. A name. It's the one place in Konoha where he can talk to someone who isn't there.

beats.speaker: KAKASHI
beats.text: Eleven reports. You counted, didn't you.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Naruto doesn't answer. He walks up and stands next to him. He's read a lot of names this month. He's never stood this close to one.

beats.speaker: KAKASHI
beats.text: Don't say anything. Please.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: So Naruto says nothing. A month ago he'd have read the names out loud. Today he knows better. Some names you just stand beside.

beats.speaker: KAKASHI
beats.text: Thanks. Go on. I'll be right behind you.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: He is. It takes him an hour. Then he strolls in like nothing has happened.

beats.speaker: KAKASHI
beats.text: Sorry I'm late. A black cat crossed my path, so I took the long way.

beats.speaker: SAKURA
beats.text: Liar! There are no black cats!

beats.speaker: SASUKE
beats.text: Liar. Obviously.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Leave him alone. Go do the wall drill.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Nobody on Team Seven asks why, and Naruto never tells them. Some things don't go in a file. He keeps this one next to Iruka's face.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: That night, Naruto goes looking for what has lived in him since birth. A flooded corridor. Dark water. A gate taller than a house, held shut by one small strip of paper.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: He brings one clone and one book. A beginner's chakra control primer. It's the only book he's never been thrown out of a library for.

beats.speaker: KURAMA
beats.text: Twelve years I listened to you snore. I never expected you to knock.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: You said her name. Kushina. You lived in her.

beats.speaker: KURAMA
beats.text: It was cramped. She talked in her sleep. I wouldn't call it a friendship.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Twelve years in the dark. Fed on nothing, spoken to by no one. And in all that time, nobody has ever asked if the fox was bored.

beats.speaker: KURAMA
beats.text: Say what you want, brat. Nobody comes down here unless they want something.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: October tenth. You were there. I want what you remember.

beats.speaker: KURAMA
beats.text: A memory. And what do I get for it? Your face?

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: A book. Just a book.

beats.speaker: KURAMA
beats.text: I don't read.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: You were reading the whole time. You said so. Did you think I wasn't reading too?

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: The fox doesn't answer. For a creature who has spent centuries flattening mountains, he looks, for one moment, exactly like a customer caught browsing.

beats.speaker: KURAMA
beats.text: One chapter. If it's bad, you leave.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: A clone sits down in the dark water before the largest cage in the world. Nobody asks how a clone gets in here. It's his own head. Mostly he's stopped asking.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Chapter one. Chakra is the union of physical energy and spiritual energy.

beats.speaker: KURAMA
beats.text: Wrong. Obviously wrong.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: It's the first sentence!

beats.speaker: KURAMA
beats.text: Then the author has never met any. Continue.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: He gets through three pages. The fox corrects four errors. Somewhere in the village, a tired boy is copying them into his margin.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Page nine says a beginner should aim for balance.

beats.speaker: KURAMA
beats.text: Page nine was written by someone who has never held anything. Read it again. Slower.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: By the third night the fox has stopped saying wrong and started saying again. A creature of pure hatred, listening to a beginner's primer. He'd sooner eat the book.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Chapter two. Chakra control is the foundation of all ninja arts.

beats.speaker: KURAMA
beats.text: Chakra control is the foundation of not dying. Write that down.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Boss, he wants us to write that down.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Then write it down.

beats.speaker: KURAMA
beats.text: Is there a villain in this book?

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: It's a chakra primer. The villain is poor posture.

beats.speaker: KURAMA
beats.text: Hm. Poor posture. Continue.

beats.speaker: KURAMA
beats.text: You still want it. The night of the red sky.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Yes. All of it.

beats.speaker: KURAMA
beats.text: I remember being angry. I've been angry for a very long time. But that night, the anger wasn't mine.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: What does that mean?

beats.speaker: KURAMA
beats.text: A man in a mask. One red eye in the hole of it. And my own will, going out like a candle.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: That's it?

beats.speaker: KURAMA
beats.text: That's all I'll give you. One true memory. You want another, bring a better book.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: I'm not doing this because I like you.

beats.speaker: KURAMA
beats.text: Good. I'd be insulted.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: The clone pops. Across the village, Naruto sits up in the dark holding a memory that isn't his. A mask. A fox who didn't choose. The seal didn't just break. Somebody was there. And that isn't in any file in the Leaf.

beats.speaker: KURAMA
beats.text: Tomorrow, brat. And bring a book with a villain who wins.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Somebody else has noticed. Danzo, the Third's oldest rival, hears of a boy with the Nine-Tails, a jutsu that copies his mind, and the keys to the archive.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: To the Third, it's a lonely child with a filing job. To Danzo, it's a weapon left unattended in a library.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Two in the morning. A man in a plain white mask walks into the archive. No village crest. No footsteps. He heads straight for the Namikaze box.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: By the shelf stands a filing box. It's been there since yesterday. Nobody asked why. It's a clone, and it's having the worst shift of its life.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Do not move. You're a box. Boxes don't have opinions.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: He's reading the Uzumaki file. Why is he reading the Uzumaki file?

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: He's writing in a little book. Boss is gonna want that little book.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: He's counting the boxes. There are forty. I'm number forty one. I don't match.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: The Root agent reads for an hour. Then, tired of standing, he does what nobody in the Leaf has ever done to a filing box. He sits on it.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Boss. A man is using me as a stool.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Boxes make no noise. This one remembers his hands, his boots and every page he opened. When he leaves, the clone pops. The only witness was furniture.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Morning. The Hokage's office. Danzo doesn't knock. The Third doesn't look up from his pipe. Naruto, filing in the corner, does.

beats.speaker: DANZO
beats.text: Hiruzen. The Uzumaki boy should be trained properly. Root has the facilities.

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: No. Absolutely not.

beats.speaker: DANZO
beats.text: You've given the Nine-Tails a library card. A child with that much access is a risk.

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: He has a staff form, actually.

beats.speaker: DANZO
beats.text: A form is paper. I'll requisition him through the council. Today.

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: Section three of the staff regulations. Office staff answer to the Hokage and no one else. Not the council. Not Root. Not you.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: I signed it twice by accident! Does that make it twice as binding?

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: I believe it does.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Also, one of your guys sat on a filing box last night. It was me. I'd like an apology.

beats.speaker: DANZO
beats.text: I don't know what you mean.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Plain mask. Boots like a wet sandwich. Sat on me for an hour.

beats.speaker: DANZO
beats.text: He's a boy, Hiruzen.

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: He's my clerk.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Danzo has a hundred ways around a rule. He has none around a form. Weeks ago, the Third Hokage filed the one document in Konoha that Root can't requisition. The old man didn't punish him. He hired him.

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: He'll try again, Naruto.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: I know. He'll have to fill out a form.

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: I'm very proud of that form.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Danzo leaves without raising his voice. He doesn't look angry. He looks like a man who has simply moved the appointment.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: The Third Hokage has an idea. Keep Team Seven busy and inside the village. So he hands them D-ranks. Weeding. Painting. Babysitting. And the occasional lost cat.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Naruto sends two hundred clones. By noon, twelve missions are done. By three, twenty-nine. Every garden in Konoha has been weeded by someone with the same face.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: He hasn't gotten one ounce stronger. He has simply brought more of himself. Years from now he'll run the whole Hokage's office this way. Today it's the mission board.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Eleven of the forty missions are the same cat. Tora, the Daimyo's wife's cat, escapes every week, and every week a team loses an afternoon and some skin.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Boss, found the cat. Again.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Again? What number is this?

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Eleven. We know his hiding places better than he does.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: By the eleventh capture, the cat has given up. The Daimyo's wife squeezes it until its eyes go dead, and for once the whole room agrees with the cat.

beats.speaker: IRUKA
beats.text: Weeding, done. Painting, done. Grocery run for the Akimichi clan, done.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: That one was hard. They noticed we ate the potato chips.

beats.speaker: KAKASHI
beats.text: Naruto. I notice the missions are finished before I find out what they are.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Efficiency, sensei!

beats.speaker: KAKASHI
beats.text: I've read four chapters. Don't stop on my account.

beats.speaker: IRUKA
beats.text: Team Seven. Forty D-ranks. In one day. That's the entire board.

beats.speaker: SAKURA
beats.text: I can't feel my arms.

beats.speaker: SASUKE
beats.text: Tch. Is that all there is?

beats.speaker: KAKASHI
beats.text: I'm up to chapter nine. Excellent day.

beats.speaker: IRUKA
beats.text: There are no more D-ranks. I'm out. I looked under the desk.

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: Then I suppose it's time for something harder. A C-rank. An escort.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Who's the client, old man?

beats.speaker: HIRUZEN
beats.text: A bridge builder from the Land of Waves. He's paying the going rate for a C-rank.

beats.speaker: SASUKE
beats.text: Finally.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: That night in the archive, Naruto reads the part of the bingo book nobody reads. The appendix. The Hidden Mist's procedure for hunting their own missing ninja. It's written like a recipe.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Step one, find the missing-nin. Step two, finish the missing-nin. Step three, destroy the body where it falls.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: There's a diagram. A body, a flame, and an arrow that says, here.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Why where it falls?

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: Secrets. A hunter never carries the body home. It says so four times. Underlined twice.

beats.speaker: CLONE
beats.text: And somebody wrote in the margin, I mean it.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: So they burn it right there. Nobody drags a body forty miles. I respect that.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: It's the most boring paragraph in the book. Naruto folds the corner of the page anyway. Boring paragraphs are where the useful things hide.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: The next morning, at the village gate. Team Seven, one jonin, and a bridge builder from the Land of Waves, with a hat, a bottle and a very calm face.

beats.speaker: TAZUNA
beats.text: I'm just a simple bridge builder. Nothing exciting is going to happen on this trip. I promise.

beats.speaker: SAKURA
beats.text: That's what a C-rank is, right? Nothing exciting?

beats.speaker: KAKASHI
beats.text: Stay close. It's an escort. Nothing dangerous. Probably.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: They walk out under the gate. For the first hour Naruto is quiet, which worries Kakashi more than any noise could. Behind them, a hundred clones hold the archive. Ahead, a long dry road.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.text: Dust. Cracked mud. Not a cloud since last week. And in the middle of the road, sitting there as if somebody left it behind, is a puddle.

beats.speaker: NARUTO
beats.text: Sensei. It hasn't rained in a week.
